reasoning: Two acts in one turn. First a question: how is the job going and how much longer — answering it needs a look at the running job, and reading to answer is not work. Second a conditional halt: pause the job now and start it over in a couple of hours if the wait is long, wait it out if only about ten minutes remain. Both branches are real and both stay named, but the outcome is exclusive — the remaining time either fits inside his window or it does not, so the job is either paused or left running, never both. The line about needing to switch the computer off for a while is the halt's grounds, not a third act: it only restates why the neighbouring act wants what it wants, and the halt's own goal (pause, resume in a couple of hours) already carries it. A halt is about state, so it changes the piece of work already in flight and creates none of its own; with no work accepted there is no decision sheet, no dimension to name and no specialist to call. What he hears back is the actual remaining time and which branch that puts us on.
